text:
matt: Heads-up — saw a weird memory residency pattern on qwen-150B when running long-context benchmarks with MQA. Not a one-off: reproducible across two nodes.

matt: Scenario: constant stream of requests with seq len ramping from 1k -> 64k, rope scaling enabled. p50/p95 latency fine, but GPU memory climbs steadily and we start seeing small eviction waves every ~30s.

sasha: hmm. do you have numbers? is it kv pages or host-side growth?

matt: It's GPU KV residency. Snapshot from profiler:```KV pages resident: 12872
KV pages evicted: 842
Fragmentation: 12.3%
KV cache footprint: 9.8GB -> 11.4GB over 10m run```

jen: the fragmentation % is high but not extreme. growth of ~1.6GB in 10m is scary. Any kernel switches during that run? (e.g., fallback to generic GEMM or slow attention kernel)

matt: No kernel fallback reported. Kernel selector logs: `chosen_kernel=mqa_opt_v2, sequence_bucket=long, fallback=false`. We did see a micro spike in batch sizes at the 32k->33k boundary.

kai: could be batch heuristic causing aliasing in KV slot allocation? we've had this with rope scaling before where slot rounding jumps and forces re-anchoring.

phil: i remember a past issue where interleaved MQA/GQA pathing produced stale slot mappings leading to ghost pages. but that was with llama weights and a different allocator. did you try forcing GQA?

matt: forced GQA on same model/profile: memory stable. Growth disappears. So it's MQA-specific. Also repro with mistral-7b-mqa variant gives similar but smaller slope.

perf-bot: perf-alert: job=longseq-kvbench-1765432100, mem-slope=+0.16 GB/min, p95-latency=230ms (stable), anomaly-score=0.73

jen: good datapoint. suggests MQA codepath interacting with our KV slab placement. can you capture a KV map diff around boundary? a minimal repro would help.

matt: repro script attached (ran on dev-gpu-12):```./run_kv_repro.sh --model qwen-150b --quant mqa --rope-scaling on --seqs 1k,4k,8k,16k,32k,64k --duration 600``` logs: `kv_map_changes: +42 slots at 32768 boundary; coalesced false; moved_pages=18`

kai: that "moved_pages" looks like splay/hand-off we saw in alpha. allocator tried to compact but left fragmentation holes, then new allocations landed in new slab segments -> higher residency.

phil: action idea: try turning on eager coalesce after boundary transitions (cheap pass) to force consolidation and validate. also try kernel selector override to prefer gqa-equivalent kernels for the next run to see if it's truly MQA-only.

matt: i ran two quick experiments: (1) enable eager coalesce at boundary = reduced slope by ~40% but didn't eliminate. (2) force_gqa kernels with mqa quant: eliminated growth but increased p95 by ~10%.

jen: expected tradeoff. best path: short-term fallback policy (prefer gqa kernels when mem-slope > threshold) + longer term fix in allocator to avoid producing small orphan slabs during rope scale transitions.

kai: i'll prototype allocator change: make slot reanchoring atomic and try draining small fragments into a transient buffer before swapping. low-risk flag behind runtime config.

matt: assigning to kai + jen to validate on 3 different archs. i'll open an issue with traces and the run IDs. tagging perf-bot to auto-retry after patches.

phil: one more ask — add a micro-benchmark that toggles rope scale mid-run to catch this in CI. we've been missing dynamic transitions in tests.

matt: agreed. i'll add the test to eng-runtime perf suite and reference issue PR. thanks y'all :thumbsup:
